question: The difference between a farmer’s output over and above his on-farm consumption is known as _________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**marketable surplus.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• It refers to the difference between the total output produced by a farmer and his on-farm consumption.
 
• In other words, it is that portion of the total output that the farmer sells in the market.
 
• **Marketable Surplus = Total farm output produced by the farmer - Own consumption of farm output.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Consumer surplus:**

 
 
• Consumer surplus is an economic measurement of consumer benefits resulting from market competition.
 
• A consumer surplus happens when the price that consumers pay for a product or service is less than the price they're willing to pay.
 
 
 
• **Foreign Consumption:**
 
 
• Most foreign publications reverse the names of modern individuals, and most Japanese reverse their own names when creating materials for foreign consumption.
 
 
 
• **Domestic Consumption:**
 
 
• Consumption is defined as the use of goods and services by a household. It is a component in the calculation of the Gross Domestic Product (GDP).
 
• Macroeconomists typically use consumption as a proxy for the overall economy.
